label: Copy-phase echo of s/w (and late-copy z/l/n/x/i/c/b)
explanation: Almost entirely a copy-phase unit (97.6% of activation mass at t > L); never fires at the delimiter or at recall_idx 0-1, and only weakly in the original phase (around t=2-3). Within the copy phase it is token-selective on the fed-back input: s and w give the strongest activations (rate ~0.31-0.33, ~58% of mass, all top examples are s or w), followed by a weaker group z, l, n, x, i, c, b. Rate climbs steadily with recall_idx / absolute step (0.02 at recall_idx 2 to 0.37 at recall_idx 8), and is highest near the end of the sequence (to_go 0-1), so late copy positions let weaker tokens cross threshold. It fires almost only on repeated (non-first) occurrences of the token, which is what being in the copy phase implies. The predicate (s/w anywhere from recall_idx 2, the weaker tokens only from recall_idx 5) gets about 0.65 precision and 0.69 recall on dev, with 84% of mass; the remaining misses are diffuse low-magnitude firings on other letters late in the copy phase.
